newsitem.title: BRAZIL: OAS head sees diplomacy returning Cuba to Americas.
newsitem.headline: OAS head sees diplomacy returning Cuba to Americas.

text.p: The secretary general of the Organisation of American States said on Thursday he believed diplomatic negotiations will gradually bring Cuba back into the Inter-American fold.

Cesar Gaviria, paying a visit to the Brazilian capital Brasilia, told reporters divergences between some Latin American countries and the United States over Cuba did not centre on objectives but on the way to reintegrate the Caribbean island.

"No doubt Cuba is the main political problem we have in this hemisphere," he said. "The differences we have are not over objectives, but over how best to reintegrate Cuba into the Inter-American system."
Cuba's membership of the OAS was suspended in 1961.

Most Latin American nations have condemned Washington's attempts to make the communist country an international pariah through its so-called Helms-Burton law, which threatens penalities against foreign firms doing business there.
On Wednesday the Rio Group of 14 Latin American countries blasted the law, which tightened an existing U.S. economic embargo.
Gaviria said he expected to see a round of heightened diplomatic efforts to bring Cuba back into the fold.
"I have great confidence we will be able to resolve this problem in the future," he said.
Gaviria also expressed confidence in the establishment of a Free Trade Area of the Americas (FTAA) by 2005, as agreed at the 1994 hemispheric summit in Miami.
He noted the end of the Cold War had ushered in greater cooperation and goodwill between the United States and the continent on its southern flank.
